_about: KnowUS source policy (owner's editorial rule, Nov 9 2026). Edit this file to change what the app may cite. A source URL is allowed only if its domain (or a parent domain) is in an allowed group below, matches official_patterns, or is the person's own campaign/official site. Everything else (any other news outlet) is treated as banned. web.archive.org links are judged by the archived URL.

pending._how: Owner decided Nov 9 2026 5:51 PM: AP, Reuters and Wikipedia are banned. Set a value to "keep" to allow it again (one-line change).

groups_kept._how: set a group to false to stop allowing it

_about_groups: official_extra = government bodies on .com/.org; party_sites = official party organizations and legislative caucus sites; campaign_sites = candidates' own sites (plus each person's own site is always allowed); social_own_accounts = a person's own social posts; reference_non_news = vote/election databases, books, archives, libraries (not news media); orgs_non_news = advocacy groups, think tanks, unions, universities, companies quoted as primary sources for their own statements/ratings; app_and_data_services = sign-in, maps, open legislative data, the app's own data repo, file hosting used by official bodies (e.g. the Colorado legislature's bill files on s3) and newsletter sign-up forms officials link to. Set a group to false in groups_kept to stop allowing it. local_gov_sites = cities', towns', counties' and townships' own official websites that are not on .gov (checked: the site loads and names the place).
